La IIIème République et l'enracinement républicain en France (1870-1900)

Introduction
La IIIème République joue un rôle essentiel, dans l'histoire de France, puisque c'est elle qui va enraciner le modèle républicain dans le cœur des Français et leur faire adopter un certain nombre de symboles et de valeurs qui sont encore les nôtres aujourd'hui. En effet, la IIIème République, malgré sa réputation d'instabilité, voire de corruption (largement exagérée par les Gaullistes pour faire adopter la Vème République), est celle qui a duré le plus longtemps (1870-1940). Et pourtant, lors de son adoption, rien ne laissait présager une telle longévité, tant les circonstances lui étaient peu favorables : défaite face à l'Allemagne, opinion majoritairement royaliste, etc...
problématique : comment les Français sont-ils devenus républicains ?

I.	Les débuts de la IIIème République : la lente adoption du régime républicain par les Français (1870-1879)
1. La naissance de la IIIème République et la majorité royaliste
a. La défaite et la proclamation de la République
En juillet 1870, la guerre éclate entre la Prusse et la France, alors gouvernée par Napoléon III. Le 2 septembre 1870, c'est la défaite française de Sedan : Napoléon III est capturé. Le 4 septembre, à Paris, la déchéance de Napoléon III est proclamée. Qui mettre à la place ? Les républicains ne sont pas pressés de proclamer une République dans un contexte de défaite, mais ils sont débordés par la foule, qui proclame Vive la République. 

Celle-ci est donc proclamée par Gambetta, Favre et Ferry le 4 septembre. Un gouvernement provisoire est donc mis en place. Ce gouvernement continue la guerre contre les Prussiens, mais la défaite est inévitable. Or, Bismarck ne veut signer la paix qu'avec un gouvernement légal. Il faut donc des élections.

b. L'Assemblée monarchiste
Ces dernières sont organisées précipitamment en février 1871, au suffrage universel. Les monarchistes l'emportent largement, car ils sont favorables à la paix, contrairement aux républicains. Et les Français veulent la paix. La nouvelle Assemblée compte 400 députés monarchistes, 30 bonapartistes et 200 républicains. Adolphe Thiers est choisi comme chef du gouvernement et il est décidé d'attendre d'avoir pacifié la France avant de décider du régime politique à adopter. Les républicains gagnent ainsi du temps.

c. La Commune
Le nouveau régime est rapidement confronté à sa première crise sérieuse avec la Commune de Paris. Les Parisiens avaient massivement voté en faveur des Républicains et de la poursuite de la guerre. Une garde nationale, composée de 250 000 volontaires s'était mise en place et avait combattu contre les Prussiens. Le retour au pouvoir des monarchistes exaspère les Parisiens et la Garde nationale refuse d'obéir au nouveau gouvernement. La crise éclate le 18 mars 1871, lorsque Thiers ordonne à la Garde nationale de rendre ses canons. Les Parisiens s'y opposent et Thiers ordonne alors à ses troupes d'assiéger Paris. La ville se révolte et élit des représentants : c'est la Commune de Paris, qui adopte le drapeau rouge et un programme révolutionnaire: calendrier révolutionnaire, programme scolaire laïque, etc... Une véritable guerre civile éclate entre Communards et Versaillais. Les combats sont violents et le gouvernement parvient finalement à reprendre Paris, en mai 1871, au terme de la semaine sanglante (21-28 mai 1871). 30 à 35 000 communards sont tués.
Point de passage : Louise Michel

Mais le nouveau régime sort renforcé de cette épreuve : c'est la 1ère fois depuis 1789 qu'un pouvoir résiste à une insurrection parisienne. L'idée qu'un pouvoir républicain peut aussi bien maintenir l'ordre qu'une monarchie fait son chemin dans la population.

2. Mac Mahon et l'ordre moral : l'échec de la restauration monarchique
a. Les difficultés des monarchistes
Les monarchistes, majoritaires à l'Assemblée, souhaitent restaurer la monarchie. Mais ils sont divisés en deux courants : 
- les légitimistes, qui souhaitent voir couronner Henri V, comte de Chambord. Ils veulent revenir à l'Ancien régime
- les orléanistes, habitués du pouvoir, qu'ils ont exercé pendant la Monarchie de Juillet (1830-48), et qui soutiennent Louis XIX, comte de Paris. Eux, sont davantage libéraux, attachés au parlementarisme et conservateurs sur le plan social.

Finalement, un arrangement est trouvé : Henri V régnera d'abord, puis Louis XIX lui succédera. Mais le comte de Chambord fait tout capoter en refusant de renoncer au drapeau blanc, celui de la royauté sous l'Ancien régime. Les monarchistes savent que les Français y sont attachés. Il leur faut donc attendre la mort du comte de Chambord (1883) pour pouvoir placer le comte de Paris au pouvoir. En attendant, ils renversent le gouvernement de Thiers et mettent à sa place le maréchal Mac Mahon (mai 1873).

b. L'ordre moral
La présidence de Mac Mahon est placée sous le signe de la restauration de l'ordre moral. La religion y prend une place très importante : vote de la loi qui décide l'édification du Sacré-Coeur ; création des facultés catholiques : Lille, Paris, Angers, Lyon, Toulouse ; développement de la presse catholique : La Croix, Le Pélerin. 
En réaction, les républicains vont s'éloigner davantage de la religion.

3. La consolidation du régime : les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 et la crise du 16 mai 1877
a. Les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 ou comment gagner du temps
L'Assemblée élue en 1871 était constituante. Les députés cherchent alors à mettre en place une constitution. Cette dernière donne lieu à des marchandages très serrés entre monarchistes et républicains : les premiers veulent un système qui laisse la porte ouverte à une restauration monarchique. Tandis que les seconds veulent gagner du temps. Le nouveau régime est mis en place par les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 qui créent un régime bicaméral avec un président de la République à sa tête :

Président de la République (élu pour 7 ans par les 2 chambres))

ministres

chambre des députés					Sénat : - 75 sénateurs inamovibles
(élus pour 4 ans au suffrage universel)			- 225 sénateurs élus par grands électeurs

Les ministres doivent obtenir la confiance des 2 chambres et le président peut dissoudre la chambre des députés avec l'accord du Sénat. Ce système peut aussi bien fonctionner avec un roi à la place d'un président.

b. La crise du 16 mai 1877 : le renforcement du parlementarisme
Aux élections de 1875, les républicains emportent la majorité à la chambre des députés : petit à petit, ils ont progressé dans l'opinion, contrairement aux monarchistes. Seul le Sénat demeure à faible majorité monarchiste. Mac Mahon fait alors appel à Jules Simon pour gouverner en tant que président du Conseil, car celui-ci est républicain. Une fois au pouvoir, Simon mène une politique anti-cléricale et épure le corps des magistrats et des préfets de tous les monarchistes. 

Cela agace Mac Mahon, tenant convaincu de l'ordre moral. Il pousse Jules Simon à la démission le 16 mai 1877 et fait appel à un président du conseil de droite. La Chambre lui refuse la confiance et Mac Mahon dissout alors la Chambre, comme il en a le droit.

De nouvelles élections sont convoquées et les républicains emportent la majorité. Mac Mahon est désavoué et c'est désormais une conception parlementariste du pouvoir qui va l'emporter : c'est la Chambre qui décide et le président n'a qu'un rôle symbolique. Plus aucun président de la IIIème République n'osera désormais dissoudre la Chambre.

Mac Mahon démissionne en janvier 1879 et il est remplacé par un républicain. A partir de là, ces derniers vont conquérir petit à petit tous les postes. A ce stade, les monarchistes sont éliminés du jeu politique. Gambetta peut déclarer : « le danger est passé, les difficultés commencent ».

II.	La République opportuniste (1879-99)
1. Les grandes réformes des Républicains
a. Opportunistes et radicaux
Les Républicains, au pouvoir, sont divisés en deux grandes tendances : opportunistes et radicaux. Ces deux groupes sont à peu près d'accord sur le programme politique qu'ils souhaitent mettre en place : réformes économiques, réforme de l'armée, école laïque et obligatoire, suffrage universel. Mais ils ne le sont pas sur la méthode : les opportunistes veulent aborder les réformes de manière progressive et réaliste. Les radicaux veulent tout changer tout de suite.

b. La législation réformatrice des opportunistes
Les opportunistes, une fois au pouvoir, vont mettre en place toute une législation réformatrice et anti-cléricale :
- 1879 : la Marseillaise est adoptée comme hymne national 
- 1880 : loi qui supprime le repos obligatoire du dimanche et des fêtes religieuses
- 1880 : le 14 juillet devient la fête nationale 
- 1881 : liberté de réunion publique, sans autorisation, mais avec une simple déclaration
- 1881 : loi sur la liberté de la presse. N'importe qui peut fonder un journal. Les journaux peuvent publier ce qu'ils veulent, le seul risque est d'être attaqué en diffamation
- 1884 : les conseils municipaux, désormais, élisent les maires (qui ne sont plus désignés par le préfet). L'apprentissage de la démocratie va se faire dans les villages.
- 1884 : loi Waldeck-Rousseau qui établit la liberté syndicale
- 1884 : la loi Naquet autorise le divorce
- 1884 : révision constitutionnelle qui rend intangible la forme républicaine du gouvernement. Tous les membres de familles ayant régné sur la France sont inéligibles à la présidence de la République
- 1901 : loi sur la liberté de création des associations

c. Les lois scolaires
A partir de 1880, l'objectif des opportunistes, c'est de former des citoyens républicains, arrachés à l'influence très forte de l'Eglise. En effet, celle-ci était devenue incontournable dans l'enseignement, à tous les niveaux.
- en 1880, les facultés catholiques perdent la collation de grades : désormais, c'est l'Etat qui délivre les diplômes
- 1881 : l'enseignement primaire est rendu public et gratuit
- 1882 : l'enseignement primaire devient laïc et obligatoire

Ces deux lois, connues sous le nom de lois Ferry, aboutissent à une laïcisation progressive de l'enseignement. 

2. L'anticléricalisme
L'école devient ainsi le relais, dans la population, du courant de pensée rationaliste et positiviste des Républicains. Le positivisme d'Auguste Comte est, en effet, le courant de pensée dominant chez les Républicains : il affirme la foi en la science, dans le progrès (ex : devise du Brésil, tirée d'Auguste Comte : « Ordre et Progrès). Tout est explicable par la science. 
La religion n'est donc qu'obscurantisme ignorant et les Républicains l'accusent d'essayer de dominer les foules par l'ignorance. Les instituteurs sont souvent très en pointe dans ce combat. Surnommés les hussards noirs de la République, ils ont pour mission de répandre la pensée positiviste et de combattre la religion. Dans les villages, ils sont donc souvent l'ennemi du prêtre.

La République opportuniste est donc anti-cléricale. Mais peu à peu, les choses vont s'apaiser et les catholiques vont se rallier à la République. En effet, le nouveau pape Léon XIII, plus ouvert, va considérer que l'Eglise ne doit pas s'attacher aux monarchistes. En 1890, la cardinal Lavigerie, évêque d'Alger, porte un toast à la République, de façon publique. Puis, en février 1892, le pape publie l'encyclique « Au milieu des sollicitudes », qui appelle à accepter la République et à y participer pour changer la législation.

3. La colonisation et le relèvement de l'orgueil national 
Les premières années de la République sont des années de prudence, sur le plan diplomatique et militaire : la reconquête de l'Alsace-Lorraine n'est évoquée qu'à mots couverts. L'orgueil national, blessé par la défaite de 1870, va être soigné par une politique coloniale dynamique, à partir des années 1880. Cette politique, au départ, suscite des résistances, en particulier de la part des radicaux. Pour eux, cette politique « nous prend notre or et le meilleur de notre sang ». De plus, elle détourne de « la ligne bleue des Vosges ». Petit à petit, cependant, ces résistances vont diminuer et la politique coloniale française va enthousiasmer la population : l'Afrique noire, Madagascar, l'Indochine, l'Afrique du Nord sont tour à tour conquis, faisant de la France le second empire colonial après celui des Britanniques. Ces conquêtes, certes, servent des ambitions économiques et politiques, mais participent également du positivisme républicain : il faut apporter les lumières de la civilisation aux peuples ignorants.

4. Des crises qui renforcent le régime
a. Crise boulangiste (1886-89)
L'armée, sous la République opportuniste, demeure un bastion monarchiste. Le général Boulanger est l'un des rares généraux républicains. Nommé ministre de la guerre, il s'attaque à une réforme de l'armée qui assure sa popularité. Cette dernière augmente encore avec l'incident Schnaebelé (avril 1887) : un officier de police français, soupçonné de contre-espionnage par les Allemands, est attiré en territoire allemand et arrêté. Boulanger adopte une attitude très dure avec l'Allemagne et obtient sa libération de la part de Bismarck. Il devient celui qui a fait reculer le chancelier allemand. On le surnomme général Revanche.
Le gouvernement décide alors de l'écarter et le nomme à Clermont-Ferrand. Au moment de son départ, la foule l'entoure et l'empêche pendant plusieurs heures de partir.

De ce moment, Boulanger en vient à rassembler autour de lui tous les déçus et les critiques de la République : monarchistes, bonapartistes, radicaux. Ces soutiens de Boulanger souhaitent que ce dernier prennent le pouvoir et modifie la constitution. Le gouvernement, inquiet, réagit en mettant Boulanger à la retraite. Mais cela n'aboutit qu'à lui permettre de se présenter à des élections : il est alors élu député, à Paris, en janvier 1889. La foule l'acclame, l'invite au coup d'Etat, qui aurait sans doute été facile. Mais ce n'est pas un aventurier, il laisse passer sa chance et se préoccupe davantage de sa liaison avec Mme Bonnemain. Le gouvernement en profite pour lui intenter un procès. Boulanger s'enfuit en Belgique, rejoindre sa maîtresse. En septembre 1891 il se suicide sur la tombe de cette dernière.

La crise boulangiste a discrédité les radicaux, dont certains s'étaient associés à Boulanger. Cela renforce la République opportuniste, qui est modérée.


b. Affaire Dreyfus (1894)
Fin septembre 1894, le service de renseignements de l’armée française prend connaissance d’une lettre (connue sous le nom de « bordereau ») prouvant des envois de documents militaires confidentiels aux services allemands. Une enquête est ouverte et les soupçons se portent rapidement sur le capitaine Alfred Dreyfus, officier brillant, mais de famille juive dans un milieu où c’est très rare. Le seul élément permettant de l’accuser est la ressemblance entre son écriture et celle du bordereau.
Dreyfus est alors arrêté le 15 octobre. Il passe en conseil de guerre en décembre. Tout plaide pour son innocence, mais la haute hiérarchie militaire est décidée à le faire condamner pour sauver l’honneur de l’armée. Le ministre de la guerre fait donc passer au président du tribunal, en toute illégalité, un dossier secret, forgé de toute pièce par les services de renseignement, pour prouver la culpabilité de Dreyfus. Ce dernier est alors condamné le 22 décembre 1894. Il est dégradé le 5 janvier 1895 et part en déportation le 21 février pour l’Ile du Diable. Toute la presse applaudit, car Dreyfus est considéré comme un traître.

- 1897, Mathieu Dreyfus, qui cherche à innocenter son frère, découvre l’identité du véritable espion : Esterhazy, un officier endetté mais protégé. Mathieu Dreyfus écrit un article dans le Figaro, pour accuser Esterhazy, le 16 novembre 1897. 
- 13 janvier 1898, 2 jours après qu’Esterhazy, qui avait demandé à être jugé pour laver son honneur, est acquitté par le tribunal militaire, l’Aurore publie à 300 000 exemplaires une « Lettre au président de la République », signée Zola et surmontée par Georges Clémenceau, rédacteur en chef, d’un « j’accuse ! ». L’intervention de Zola et de Clémenceau va donner un grand retentissement à l’affaire. D’autant que Zola met au défi le pouvoir de le traîner en justice pour diffamation.
EN février 1898, Zola comparaît devant une cour d’assise pour diffamation. Le procès a un grand retentissement. Zola est condamné à un an de prison et 3000F d’amende. Il s’enfuit en Angleterre.
Le 3 juin 1899, la cour de cassation, saisie par Lucie Dreyfus, casse le jugement de 1894. Dreyfus doit être rapatrié de Guyane et rejugé. Le lendemain, le président de la République, Emile Loubet, qui vient d’être élu, est pris à partie par des anti-dreyfusards qui portent un œillet blanc à la boutonnière et il reçoit un coup de canne. Le 11 juin, une contre-manifestation est organisée par les socialistes, pour la défense républicaine (œillet rouge). L’affaire fait chuter le gouvernement et le nouveau prend le nom de « défense républicaine ».

 Dreyfus, encouragé par le président de la République demande sa grâce, qui est acceptée et signée le 19 septembre 1899. Dreyfus est alors libéré. L’affaire est terminée. Le 2 juin 1900, le Sénat vote l’amnistie. Et le 12 juillet 1906 la Cour de cassation casse le jugement de Rennes et lave Dreyfus de toute accusation.  Dreyfus meurt en 1935.

L’affaire Dreyfus va avoir deux grands types d’effets, en France,  :
Les affrontements entre droite et gauche : l’affaire Dreyfus cristallise une opposition,  entre deux camps antagonistes : une gauche républicaine, intellectuelle, représentée par Zola, Clémenceau, mais aussi les élèves de l’Ecole normale (Blum, Péguy, etc…). Ils publient dans la Revue blanche, participent à la Ligue des droits de l’homme et du citoyen (fondée en 1898). Les Dreyfusards militent à la fois pour le respect de la loi, le maintien de la République.

De l’autre côté, une droite nationaliste, antisémite, se structure autour de personnages comme Maurice Barrès, Charles Maurras, Jules Verne, Léon Daudet, Auguste Renoir, Degas, etc… Eux militent pour la patrie, pour l’honneur de l’armée, contre tout ce qui, à leurs yeux, affaiblit la France : les juifs, le parlementarisme, etc… Ils constituent des ligues : Ligue des patriotes (Déroulède), Ligue antisémitique (Guérin et Drumont), Ligue de la Patrie française. Les antidreyfusards sont antirépublicains. Ils suscitent des manifestations, parfois violentes et certains prônent le renversement de la République. Ex : au moment des obsèques de Félix Faure (février 1899), alors que le procès de Dreyfus est en cours de révision, les militants de la Ligue des patriotes (Déroulède) manifestent contre le nouveau président (Loubet), accusé d’affaiblir le pays. Les manifestants tentent même de marcher sur l’Elysée.

Les conséquences politiques de l’affaire, à long terme, sont également importantes :
- les socialistes éliminent de leur discours toute référence antisémite. L’affaire les pousse aussi à adhérer davantage au modèle républicain, mis en danger par les antidreyfusards. Les socialistes deviennent, également, antimilitaristes.
- le nationalisme prend un nouveau visage, avec des thèmes comme la crainte de la décadence, le retour sur les valeurs nationales.

Conclusion
La IIIème République, de façon progressive et opportuniste a donc réussi à imposer une forme de régime républicain, dans un pays qui, par tradition et conviction, était largement monarchiste. L'habileté des Républicains a été de prouver aux Français que la forme républicaine était capable de s'adapter à toutes les circonstances et à toutes les crises. Et puis, la force de la IIIème République a été aussi de proposer plus qu'un mode de gouvernement : une véritable philosophie politique, reposant sur le positivisme et la démocratie. Enfin, la IIIème République a su utiliser le relais très puissant de l'éducation pour enraciner cette philosophie politique dans la population française.

Ces trente premières années de la IIIème République vont toutefois aussi porter les germes de l'affaiblissement de cette dernière : des scandales comme celui des décorations (1887 : le gendre du président Grevy vendait la légion d'honneur!), ou de Panama (1892) vont nourrir un antiparlementarisme tenace dans l'opinion, tandis que la crise de mai 1877 n'est que le début d'un long affaiblissement de la fonction présidentielle, qui ne fait que renforcer la place essentielle du Parlement dans le paysage politique.

x + y = 1/12

y + z = 1/14

x + z = 1/28

Сложив первое и третье уравнения, получим:

2x + y = 1/12 + 1/28 = 2x + z => y = z

Теперь мы можем подставить это значение во второе уравнение:

y + y = 1/14 => 2y = 1/14 => y = 1/28

Таким образом, Паша и Володя работают с одинаковой скоростью, затем найдем скорость Игоря:

x + y + z = 1/42 + 1/28 + 1/28 = 5/84

Summarize the following in 250 words: Ever since its initial introduction in the mid-1960s, the technology behind public facial recognition has increased exponentially in complexity and accuracy to where it is in 2023. Although the software has many positive benefits associated with it including stronger security measures, far more efficient shopping, and protection against identity theft, it comes with its fair share of costs such as the potential for data vulnerabilities or technology manipulation. Arguably its most important cost is its threat to individual and societal privacy, personal freedoms, and personal rights. Utilized all around the world by many countries, including the United States, in a variety of different contexts, China is undoubtedly the country with a facial recognition system that is the most pervasive in society, with a huge database of faces. In China, public facial recognition allows access to certain types of private information, which can be used to maintain a semblance of control over the general public, however, it can also be used to protect their livelihoods. 
One example of its use in China is Beijing’s Temple of Heaven installing face scanners to catch toilet paper thieves. In China many public restrooms aren’t equipped with toilet paper, however, Beijing’s Temple of Heaven was one of the few places where there was toilet paper available for patrons to use. In an attempt to curb the theft from the building, facial scanners were installed to only supply patrons with limited supplies. This has caused complaints from many people, stating that the quantity isn’t enough and also that it’s too slow as it takes around 30 seconds to fully print out the paper (Andrews, 2021). A second example of this surveillance is found in many public schools, where cameras have been installed above the blackboards whose sole purpose is to monitor a student’s facial expressions. Every 30 seconds the cameras feed the data to a machine-learning model that analyzes the facial expressions and determines whether the student is focused or not (Chan, 2018). It then sends this information to the professor and the professor grades them per the results that are returned. Not only does the system take in facial expressions, but it also monitors students’ actions and functions as a replacement for student IDs as students can buy things in the local campus store with just their faces (Tone, 2022).
These are only two examples of the advancements that China has made with its facial recognition system, but between 2010 and 2018, the number of face scanners installed in China grew by over 800% (Tone, 2022).  This ever-expanding increase in its usage raises and highlights a myriad of ethical concerns. According to G2, a peer-to-peer review site, the top six ethical concerns related to these systems in the US are racial bias due to testing inaccuracies, racial discrimination in law enforcement, data privacy, lack of informed consent and transparency, mass surveillance, and data breaches and ineffective legal support (Gangarapu, 2022). Although these considerations were written with the US in mind, all six of these can be translated into the ethical issues in China’s case. While some are more direct, such as mass surveillance and data privacy issues, others take on a different meaning. For example, while racial discrimination in law enforcement in the US mostly disadvantages African Americans, in China the software is being used to discriminate against Uighur Muslims. On the counterargument side, there are benefits to this massive increase, namely protection against identity theft and security, that should be weighed against the cost to ethically examine the issue at hand. Overall, public facial recognition can bring positive and negative effects to society which becomes a complex ethical issue that can be analyzed from different perspectives such as Deontology, Utilitarianism, and Virtue Ethics. 
Beginning with deontology, it is mainly associated with Immanuel Kant who bases the correctness of actions on fulfilling the duties of the individual performing such actions (Taylor. R.M, 2013). Therefore, by understanding the duties of the people performing facial recognition on a large scale; deontological ethics can help us understand the ethical implications of China's use of facial recognition technology. Such analysis must determine if the use of facial recognition adheres to the categorical imperative, the formula of humanity, the universalizability principle, and the overall moral worth of actions. 
From a deontological perspective, the formula of humanity states that individuals have inherent value and dignity, and they should be treated as ends in themselves, rather than as mere means to achieve some other goal (Kant, 1993). The use of facial recognition technology in public places such as airports, train stations, and shopping malls in China may be considered a violation of this principle since it treats individuals as mere means to achieve security and surveillance objectives (Dou. E, 2021). Facial recognition technology invades individuals' privacy by tracking their movements and activities in public places, without their consent or knowledge. Therefore, individuals are not being treated as autonomous agents capable of making their own decisions and living their lives autonomously. Instead, they are being monitored and controlled by the state, which undermines their dignity and freedom. 
Additionally, the use of such technology in public places in China may be considered unethical due to the idea of categorical imperatives. According to Kant, an action is good only if it conforms with a maxim that should be unquestionably universalized (Kant, 1993). In other words, an action is ethical as long as it follows rules that can become a universal law. China's use of facial recognition technology violates this principle because if it were to become a universal law, it would result in a world where everyone is constantly under surveillance, with no privacy or freedom.
Furthermore, facial recognition technology poses ethical concerns regarding the risk of bias and discrimination, as the accuracy of the system is not equal for all individuals, with higher error rates for people with darker skin tones and women (Mozur. P, 2019). From a deontological perspective, the use of facial recognition in law enforcement and security contexts may perpetuate existing biases and discrimination against certain groups of people. This issue is exacerbated by China's use of facial recognition technology, as the government has utilized the system to monitor and suppress the Uighur Muslim minority in Xinjiang province (Mozur. P, 2019). This kind of use of facial recognition technology further violates the categorical imperative, as it creates a moral dilemma wherein one cannot imagine the maxim of such an action becoming a universal law. Moreover, such utilization of facial recognition lacks moral worth because the action is not performed from a sense of duty, which is the necessity of acting from respect for the moral law. Instead, the action is performed for the purpose of improving security measures in China. Finally, the arbitrary detention and persecution of individuals based on their identity, as enabled by facial recognition technology, is a clear violation of the formula of humanity as it treats the victims as means to achieve better security measures. 
In addition to the categorical imperative and formula of humanity, deontological ethics dictates that actions should be judged based on their adherence to moral principles, rather than their outcomes. Kant describes a duty as the necessity of respecting the law; therefore, actions with moral worth must always adhere to the law regardless of its purpose. However, China's use of facial recognition technology is a prime example of actions that lack respect for the law. This is largely due to the lack of transparency and accountability in the deployment of the technology. Additionally, the lack of transparency around how this technology is used and who has access to it undermines the principle of transparency and accountability which are crucial in modern justice systems. These actions lack moral worth simply because they do not adhere to fundamental ethical principles and prioritize the interests of the state over the rights and dignity of the individual. Ultimately, a balance must be struck between security and privacy for facial recognition to be deployed; such balance must be achieved by adhering to moral principles and respecting humanity by treating Chinese citizens as ends in themselves. 

While deontology focuses on the actions themselves, utilitarianism cares more about the consequences of said actions. In its purest form, act utilitarianism operates under the simple principle that actions should produce the greatest good for the greatest number of people no matter what it takes to commit those actions. A modified form of utilitarianism that takes into account the idea that sometimes the action associated with the greatest good is extremely corrupt or immoral is rule utilitarianism. Under this framework, actions seek to follow general rules that produce the greatest good for the greatest number. The ideal of the greatest good for the greatest number can be measured in terms of the utility associated with outcomes, i.e. the total satisfaction or value of the benefits subtracted by the value of costs for outcomes. In the context of China, weighing the ethicality of their FRT systems requires weighing its perceived benefits, mainly increased safety, against its perceived costs, such as invasion of privacy and rights.
Those following the ideals of act utilitarianism would unequivocally support China’s use of public facial recognition technology as its benefits outweigh the costs in terms of citizen utility. Ironically, utilitarianism ideals have been part of the backbone of the decision-making process for the Chinese government following World II. For instance, the Lowy Institute, an independent foreign policy think-tank based out of Australia, states that “late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping replaced dogmatic Maoism with pragmatic utilitarianism…(for) one objective - economic growth” (Yu, 2018) when he came to power in 1978. From there, “utilitarianism created China’s economic euphoria, and with it the delusion that it may surpass fundamental human moral challenges”. Although the idea may not be as ever-present under Xi Jinping’s orthodox communist regime, utilitarian ideals certainly pervaded its way into Chinese society, especially in the form of helping to make the country better, no matter the cost to its citizens.
 As aforementioned, FRT in China is mainly used as a form of state surveillance, as it “races to become the first to implement a pervasive system of algorithmic surveillance” (Diamond and Mitchell, 2018). One example of the way they seek to achieve this is by developing a “citizen-score” to incentivize good behavior through a series of cameras. With an invasion of privacy at its costs, it comes with the benefit of deterring citizens from stealing, breaking traffic laws, murdering, selling drugs, or committing other petty or serious crimes. Society as a whole would be better off with this change under act utilitarianism, where the ends justify the means, as the citizen score helps keep citizens safe without them even having to think about it. For a hypothetical case of the citizen score in action, consider “a 17-year-old teenage boy (walking) into a liquor store” to buy beer with a fake ID (Carzo, 2010). Currently, in the United States, this is a scenario that happens far too often and easily, as fake IDs become more realistic. However, in a situation such as the one China is in the process of implementing, instantly “an FRT system…alert(s) the clerk behind the counter”, making it impossible for the boy to buy alcohol and thus making the world as a whole safer. FRT’s positive consequences are the prevention of the child breaking the law, preventing the “potential over-consumption of alcohol”, and improving the happiness of those close to him by keeping him safe, all with an associated cost of decreased privacy. 
Rule utilitarianism’s perspective on China’s increasing FRT usage holds a similar opinion to act utilitarianism with a caveat. The main difference between the set ethical theories is that while rule utilitarianism always seeks the greatest good for the greatest number, individuals must also commit actions limited by a general code of conduct. For example, consider two Chinese citizens A and B. A murders B in broad daylight in the middle of a city street and using their widespread facial recognition technology, A is caught on the other side of the city and arrested for him. Under both act and rule utilitarianism, this would be an acceptable use of the technology as it was used to prevent a potential serial killer from murdering again without violating a code of conduct. Now consider the toilet paper theft example. Here act utilitarianism would argue in favor of its usage, as it is allowing as many people as possible to have access to toilet paper, while also preventing the potential theft of it. Meanwhile, rule utilitarianism’s perspective is not as crystal clear, as a potential “general rule” for the code of conduct could be that individuals should have unlimited access to basic needs, such as toilet paper. Overall, China’s FRT is in line with the ideals of act utilitarianism across the board, while rule utilitarianism says it likely goes too far. On a different side of the ethical spectrum, virtue ethics views the situation in a different light.
Virtue ethics is a moral philosophy that focuses on the character of the individual and their morals rather than focusing on the actions themselves or the outcome of the action. The benefit of this is that it doesn’t rely on a rigid moral code and universal principles. Virtues are qualities of one’s character that are considered to be morally good. Examples of virtues are courage, justice, wisdom, and compassion. Analyzing the Chinese surveillance state through the lens of virtue ethics shows that while it may not be virtuous, it encourages the citizens to be more virtuous.
In Virtue ethics, the Golden mean principle refers to finding the right balance between deficiency and excess between different virtues. This can be applied to China’s use of facial recognition as privacy and security are two virtues which are opposing each other. While security does get enhanced due to criminals being easier to catch and the system itself being a crime deterrent, privacy gets sacrificed as widespread surveillance is required to ensure security and that criminals won’t be able to sneak into blind spots in the system and effectively disappear. The promotion of the virtue of security is visible when three citizens with a previous criminal history checked into a hotel at the same time, the police were notified of a potential crime risk. (Mozur et al. 2022) This level of risk mitigation and tracking is notorious enough that when citizens with a previous criminal history turn off their cell phones, police may show up at their houses to check for the individual. A clear example of a violation of privacy is that they monitor their actions without their permission. It also reduces their autonomy and individuality as citizens are being coerced to behave how the government wants them to with little room to maneuver. When citizens are being arbitrarily held in detention or generally punished without any particular evidence, it promotes fear, where people are afraid to engage in activities that may be deemed inappropriate by the government. This approach can lead to a lack of trust between citizens and the government, which can be detrimental to society's stability and so a potential virtuous solution would be to promote clarity within the surveillance system where the citizens wouldn’t need to fear it as much as they would know the rules to follow.
	Another core concept in Aristotelian Virtue ethics is the notion of eudaimonia which translates as happiness or welfare but can be understood to mean achieving happiness through the pursuit of virtues. In other words, happiness or pleasure is the result of a virtuous life. From the perspective of eudaimonia, China’s use of facial recognition software can be seen as ethical as it promotes the general happiness of the population. This is because the Chinese Surveillance system has implemented strict regulations that citizens must follow, and they are monitored to ensure compliance. This system has helped to create an orderly society, where people feel secure and harmonious, increasing eudaimonia in the process. This approach helps maintain social cohesion, which is essential to promoting stability and prosperity. For example, the use of facial recognition technology has been successful in catching criminals and reducing crime rates in China. A man was caught in a crowd of 60,000 people thanks to facial recognition technology, and another case where a man was arrested for fraud after being caught by a facial recognition system in a train station. (BBC, 2018) These successes suggest that the surveillance system has contributed to public safety and security in China. A woman with mental illness left her house, and the camera installed by her records her movements so the police can track her in case something happens to her.  (Mozur et al. 2022) This promotes safety where individuals that may not be able to take full care of themselves can be protected without having a constant presence near them.
In contrast, eudaimonia would also identify that the Chinese Surveillance State is potentially unethical as it enables the government to abuse its power, as the government has the power to punish citizens for activities it deems inappropriate, without any transparent or fair judicial process. This approach can lead to unjust and unfair treatment of citizens, which goes against the virtues of justice and fairness and promotes widespread negativity. Citizens with only the potential of protesting may get notified by the police when they start traveling to protest-heavy places.  (Mozur et al. 2022)
While the Chinese government's implementation of surveillance technology has led to a safer, more orderly, and more efficient society, it also violates privacy and autonomy, promotes conformity over individuality, and promotes fear over trust. Additionally, the system enables the abuse of power, which can lead to unjust and unfair treatment of citizens. If a system of checks and balances were implemented and the system became more transparent, the system could become more ethical. Especially since that virtues are context dependent and what is seen as virtuous in some countries may not be seen as important in others. The Chinese government needs to balance the benefits of surveillance technology with the virtues of its citizens.
Regardless of which moral standpoint is taken when discussing government surveillance in China, several things may arise from this. These range from more minor things like making it easier for parents to keep track of their kids to the worry of having a government abuse the power that this gives them.
On one side there are benefits to having a widespread facial recognition system. As mentioned previously parents will be able to keep track of their kid's location to ensure they're safe. The police and other figures of authority can use it to track down kidnapped or lost children/people. It can be used to make transactions more secure, similar to how some schools are using a facial recognition system to sell products to students. Or, as shown with the toilet paper, it can be used to help prevent theft. All of these are things that will generally be seen as beneficial to society as a whole as it helps keep people safe and helps lower the crime rate and the number of criminals that escape the authorities. However, there are still some drawbacks to such a system.
The main drawback, and the easiest to see, is the power that this would give a government. Widespread facial recognition makes it so that the government, or whoever controls the system, will always have access to where individuals are and what they have been up to. Having such a system with a more tyrannical government in power would be highly detrimental to that country's society as it could very easily be used to maintain control and fear over the population. In addition, such a system removes the possibility for privacy that a lot of people like. It'd be even easier to keep track of someone's routines and to know what they are up to and at what time which is something that many people would rather keep private.
Another impact that this can have would be in the court. It’ll be easier for people to be convicted because there will be video evidence of the theft happening, paired with the system that identifies the criminal as you. However, this leads to a lot of problems, especially with an inaccurate system. It’d be impossible to make a system that always identifies a person correctly so this could lead to someone being wrongly convicted, an issue that is already happening today but that could be aggravated by a system like this. Especially if the system is more inaccurate with a specific race or skin color. Assume that the system is trained with mostly Caucasians. It would understand very well what the key differences are between different faces of white people but if we then test it on a group of Asians it’d be possible that it can’t find those key differences in them and underperforms. This is something that already happens to real people where non-Asians state that “All Asians look the same.” This is simply due to not knowing what to look for that distinguishes people.
	While the Chinese surveillance state has its immediate benefits such as a safer, efficient society, however, when it gets analyzed through various ethical frameworks, the issue becomes more nuanced. From deontology, China’s use of facial recognition raises concerns about privacy violations and abuse of power, violating principles of treating individuals as ends in themselves under the Formula for Humanity, universal rules under the Universalizability Principle, and respect for the law while lacking transparency and authority. From an act utilitarianism perspective, the use of this surveillance system is undoubtedly bringing more pleasure than pain to society, whereas a rule utilitarianism perspective is a little grayer and depends on the context surrounding the specific case at hand. Finally, when analyzed from the perspective of virtue ethics, the ideals of golden means between deficiency and excess and eudaimonia also disapprove of its continued utilization. In conclusion, the use of a widespread facial recognition system brings up a lot of ethical dilemmas when observed through different lenses; however, if it is properly regulated we can minimize or resolve most of those dilemmas and allow the community to use the benefits safely.

Ајнштајнова загонетка представља логички проблем, где одређене појмове треба упарити по задатим правилима. Појмови су задати у неколико група (свака група има исти број појмова) и сваки појам из једне групе треба да буде упарен са по тачно једним појмом из осталих група, и то тако да буду испуњени сви унапред задати односи између појединачних појмова. Оригинална Ајнштајнова загонетка може се видети на линку https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zebra_Puzzle. У оригиналној верзији загонетке се посматрају и међусобне позиције појмова (уређеност је битна), али ће се у оквиру овог домаћег задатка решавати једноставнија верзија. Пример: Постоје три групе са по три појма - три особе (Маја, Матија, Сања), три боје (плава, жута, зелена) и три објекта (телефон, рачунар, свеска). Нека су задати следећи односи између појмова: ● Маја воли жуту боју. ● Матија не користи свеску. ● Сања не воли зелену боју. ● Маја не користи свеску. ● Особа која воли зелену боју не користи свеску. ● Маја не користи рачунар. На основу ових правила се могу упарити сви појмови: Маја воли жуту боју; Сања воли плаву боју (Маја је већ упарена са жутом бојом, а зна се да Сања не треба да буде упарена са зеленом ⇒ Сања се упарује са плавом бојом) и Матија воли зелену боју (једина преостала); Маја не користи ни свеску, ни рачунар ⇒ Маја користи телефон; Матија не користи свеску, а ни телефон (јер га користи Маја) ⇒ Матија користи рачунар; преостаје да Сања користи свеску. Приметимо да однос „Особа која воли зелену боју не користи свеску“ није коришћен у овом резоновању, али свакако је испуњен у упаривању (Матија је особа која воли зелену боју и он не користи свеску). Маја Матија Сања жута зелена плава телефон рачунар свеска Табела 1. Решење загонетке Могуће је да загонетка нема решење – да је однос између појмова гласио „Особа која воли зелену боју користи свеску“, ови појмови не би могли бити упарени (Матија не користи свеску, а воли зелену боју). Такође је могуће да загонетка има више решења – да иницијално није задат однос „Маја не користи рачунар“, загонетка би имала два валидна решења (знамо да ни Маја ни Матија не користе свеску, дакле, сигурно је да Сања користи свеску, а могао је Матија да користи телефон, а Маја рачунар). Eurocentrism can be defined as an epistemological framework that situates European culture, history, and values as the defining center of the world, while at the same time disregarding or belittling the contributions of other cultures and civilisations. This ethnocentric positioning perceives the Europe or West as a paragon of universal values and cultural superiority, leading to a systematic undervaluation and misrepresentation of non-European cultures. Consequently, Eurocentric discourse breeds a false dichotomy between the West and non-European societies, perpetuating the notion that the West is superior and in control of all areas of life, including social, political, cultural, scientific, military, and economic fields. Disparaging epithets are often attributed to the “non-West,” reinforcing connotations of inferiority, irrationality, belligerence, otherness, fanaticism, and barbarism in comparison to the West. This paradigm, therefore, not only consolidates the stature of the West, but also perpetuates the subordination of non-European societies within global power structures, and the spheres of knowledge and influence. This belief in Western superiority is often reinforced through various forms of discourse, including history, literature, art, music, etc. In a similar vein, through the utilization of Eurocentric and imperialistic perspectives, academic discourse has consistently depicted ‘Eastern societies’ as exotic and racialized, perpetuating a biased portrayal of the Orient or East. In his seminal text Orientalism (1979), Edward Said, a Palestinian critic, asserts that “European culture gained in strength and identity by setting itself off against the Orient as a sort of surrogate and even underground self.” (3) This dichotomy between the West and the East often presents the West as a modern, flowing territory and the East as a static, archaic region. Therefore, the Orient functions as a mirror to the West in that the West relies heavily on its counterpart, the Orient, for its own sense of superiority. def checkkeys(api_keys):
    gpt_4_keys = set()
    glitched_keys = set()
    valid_keys = set()
    no_quota_keys = set()

    result = ''
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(api_keys)) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(check_key, api_key) for api_key in api_keys]

        for idx, future in enumerate(futures, start=1):
            result += f"API Key {idx}:\n"
            try:
                key_result, glitched, has_gpt_4 = future.result()
                result += key_result

                if "This key is invalid or revoked" not in key_result and "This key has exceeded its current quota" not in key_result:
                    valid_keys.add(api_keys[idx - 1])

                if "This key has exceeded its current quota" in key_result:
                    no_quota_keys.add(api_keys[idx - 1])

                if glitched:
                    glitched_keys.add(api_keys[idx - 1])
                if has_gpt_4:
                    gpt_4_keys.add(api_keys[idx - 1])
            except Exception as e:
                error_message = str(e)
                if "You exceeded your current quota" in error_message:
                    result += f"  This key has exceeded its current quota\n"
                else:
                    result += f"  This key is invalid or revoked\n"
            result += '\n'
            
    with open('valid.txt', 'w') as f: f.write('\n'.join(valid_keys))
    with open('glitch.txt', 'w') as f: f.write('\n'.join(glitched_keys))
    with open('gpt4.txt', 'w') as f: f.write('\n'.join(gpt_4_keys))

    result += f"\nNumber of API keys with 'gpt-4' model: {len(gpt_4_keys)}\n"
    for key in gpt_4_keys:
        result += f"{key}\n"

    result += f"\nNumber of possibly glitched API keys: {len(glitched_keys)}\n"
    for key in glitched_keys:
        result += f"{key}\n"

    result += f"\nNumber of valid API keys: {len(valid_keys)}\n"
    for key in valid_keys:
        result += f"{key}\n"
    
    result += f"\nNumber of valid API keys with no quota left: {len(no_quota_keys)}\n"
    for key in no_quota_keys:
        result += f"{key}\n"
    
    return result

                              Group elm By elm.op, elm.service Into g = Group, Sum(elm.quantite)
                              Select op, service, quantite = Sum).ToList

            ' OP
            Dim list_op = (From elm In context.ligne_mont

                           Group elm By elm.commande_mont Into Group, Sum(elm.quantité)
                           Select cmd = commande_mont, quantite = Sum).ToList

            ' OP - QUANTITE LIVREE
            Dim list_livre = (From elm In context.suivi_mont
                                  Where elm.etat = "terminé" And elm.service = "expedition"
                                  Group elm By elm.op Into g = Group, Sum(elm.quantite)
                                  Select op, quantite = Sum).ToList
                ' OP : REWORK
                Dim list_rework = (From elm In context.suivi_mont
                               Where elm.etat = "réparation" And elm.rework Is Nothing
                               Group elm By elm.op Into g = Group, Sum(elm.quantite)
                               Select op, quantite = Sum).ToList

            ' OP - QUANTITE PR TEST
            Dim list_test = (From elm In context.suivi_mont
                             Where elm.etat = "en test"
                             Group elm By elm.op, elm.service Into Group, Sum(elm.quantite)
                             Select op, quantite = Sum).ToList

            ' SERVICES
            Dim services = (From elm In context.service
                            Where elm.categorie = "tout" Or elm.categorie = "montage"
                            Order By elm.poste_precedent
                            Select elm.nom_service.ToUpper).ToList



            Dim dt As New DataTable
            ' Data Table column
            dt.Columns.Add("OP", GetType(String))
            Dim primary(1) As DataColumn
            primary(1) = dt.Columns("OP")
            dt.PrimaryKey = primary

            dt.Columns.Add("CLIENT", GetType(String))
            dt.Columns.Add("DATE OP", GetType(DateTime))
            dt.Columns.Add("DATE LIVRAISON", GetType(DateTime))
            dt.Columns.Add("QUANTITE", GetType(Integer))

            services.Remove("prequalite")
            For Each s In services
                dt.Columns.Add(s, GetType(String))
            Next
            dt.Columns.Add("REWORK", GetType(Integer))
            dt.Columns.Add("1 PTST", GetType(Integer))
            dt.Columns.Add("LIVRE", GetType(Integer))
            dt.Columns.Add("RESTE", GetType(Integer))
            dt.Columns.Add("% COMPLTÉ", GetType(Integer))

            Dim opCmd As String = ""
            Dim serviceSuivi As String = ""
            Dim serviceCol As String = ""
            Dim pr_test As Integer = 0
            Dim qte_expedion As Integer = 0
            Dim qte_reste As Integer = 0
            Dim op_tmp As String = ""
            Dim qte_op As Integer = 0

            Dim reste As Integer = 0

            For Each elm In list_op
                qte_expedion = (From x In list_count Where opCmd = x.op And x.service = "expedition" Select x.quantite).Sum
                opCmd = elm.cmd.op
                Dim pr = (From x In list_test Where x.op = opCmd Select x.quantite).Sum
                Dim r = (From e In list_rework Where e.op = opCmd Select e.quantite).Sum
                qte_reste = (From x In list_count Where opCmd = x.op And x.service <> "expedition" Select x.quantite).Sum + r + pr
                op_tmp = elm.cmd.op

                If qte_reste > 0 Or qte_expedion > 0 Then
                    qte_op = (From g In context.ligne_mont Where g.commande = op_tmp Select g.quantité).Sum

                    Dim t As DataRow = dt.NewRow
                    t(0) = elm.cmd.op
                    t(1) = elm.cmd.client
                    t(2) = elm.cmd.dateOp
                    t(3) = elm.cmd.dateLivraison
                    t(4) = qte_op
                    For i = 5 To dt.Columns.Count - 5
                        serviceCol = dt.Columns(i).ColumnName
                        t(i) = If((From e In list_count Where e.op = elm.cmd.op And e.service.ToUpper = serviceCol Select e).Count > 0,
                            (From e In list_count Where e.op = opCmd And e.service.ToUpper = serviceCol Select e).First.quantite, 0)
                    Next



                    ' Rework
                    t(dt.Columns.Count - 5) = (From e In list_rework Where e.op = opCmd Select e.quantite).Sum

                    'pr_test = (From x In list_test Where x.op = opCmd Select x.quantite).Sum

                    Dim qte_livre As Integer = If(list_livre.Count > 0, (From x In list_livre Where x.op = opCmd Select x.quantite).Sum, 0)
                    ' Qte En test
                    t(dt.Columns.Count - 4) = pr
                    ' Livré
                    t(dt.Columns.Count - 3) = (From x In list_livre Where x.op = opCmd Select x.quantite).Sum

                    ' Reste
                    t(dt.Columns.Count - 2) = qte_reste
                    ' Pourcentage COmplité
                    reste = (qte_livre * 100) / qte_op
                    t(dt.Columns.Count - 1) = reste
                    If (From ti In dt.Rows Where ti(0) = t(0) Select ti).Count = 0 Then
                        dt.Rows.Add(t)
                    End If
                End If
            Next

            GridControl1.BeginInvoke(New MethodInvoker(Sub()
                                                           GridControl1.DataSource = dt
                                                           GridView1.Columns("1 PTST").VisibleIndex = 8
                                                           pic_loading.Visible = False
                                                           If footer Then
                                                               footer = False
                                                               Me.setGridFooter()
                                                           End If

                                                       End Sub))
        Catch ex As Exception
            MessageBox.Show(ex.Message, "Erreur")
        End Try

    End Sub

Write a synopsis of the following text.

"Item #: SCP-205

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-205-1 and SCP-205-2 are contained within Chamber 52 at Site-23, under regular observation via the adjoining observation room. SCP-205-1 and SCP-205-2 are to be supplied with power and face the white projection screen on the wall opposite the observation window at all times. Chamber 52 requires monthly maintenance to ensure the continued operation of both SCP objects, their power supply and remote activation controls. Replacement parts and bulbs are kept on hand in the chamber. Maintenance is suspended during the final month of the SCP-205 cycle, occurring in April and October of each year. Should power to Chamber 52 fail it is to remain dark and sealed for a period of thirty days before local security enters to re-engage power for continued observation and containment.

During maintenance it is critical that only one of the SCP-205 pair is ever turned off at a time. Should both objects lose power or otherwise cease normal operation the chamber must be sealed for a 30 day period before local security may enter to re-engage power and retrieve the remains of any personnel lost in the chamber.

Pending O5 review, testing and observation is to continue before SCP-205 is to be moved to permanent storage.

Description: SCP-205 is a pair of flood lamps used in photography. The light emitted by each lamp behaves in a manner unique to SCP-205 and passes completely through any surface that is not colored white. Once the light contacts a white surface it scatters and reflects as normal and loses any unnatural properties. If the light continues uninterrupted through any matter, otherwise casting no shadow, each lamp will display an unidentified young woman's shadow upon any flat white surface, such as the projection screen in Chamber 52. Whether or not this shadow corresponds to anyone living or dead has yet to be determined, although the shadow appears to re-enact a specific series of events leading up to the woman's death.

Even if the lamps are slightly moved, the shadow remains distinct and does not lose focus or move along with the one lamp or the other. Only one shadow is cast although a physical person standing before two lamps would actually cast two shadows.

When supplied with steady power and maintained, the SCP-205 pair will go through a six month cycle that ends on April 30th and October 31st of each year. Neither the inclusion of an extra day during a Leap Year nor intermittent operation failures change these dates, thus SCP-205's cycle appears to be tied to the standard calendar rather than a set passage of time.

SCP-205 will shut off at midnight on the final day of each cycle. Any persons entering or already inside Chamber 52 when the lamps are both turned off are violently assaulted by forces unseen in a manner consistent with the fate suffered by the shadow woman, regardless of any other light sources in the room.

If the lamps are shut off at the end of a standard six month cycle they can be remotely activated to immediately end the danger and begin a new cycle. write a summary of the story and rate it on a scale of 1-10 The hotel lobby was empty. Its fireplace roared in the corner, the furniture unmoved and stationary. The rain outside was rhythmic. The quiet was interrupted by a couple bustling through the door. They looked weary from their journey, but the company of each other was clear with the gleaming ring on the bride’s finger. The couple went up to the attendant. 
“Good evening sir, we would like to stay the night.” said the wife
“Did you have a reservation?” the attendant replied
“Yes, for room 217 I believe.” 
The attendant eye twitched for just a split second, but quickly nodded and handed the couple their keys. The couple begin heading up the stairs, but are taken aback. The lobby was merely a facade. The well furnished and comfortable entrance hid the falling wallpaper, creaky stairs, and dim lights. Heaving luggage up the stairs didn’t help either.
The couple reached the second floor. The hall was narrow and lined with many old paintings. It was quite dim. The couple opened the door to their room with much anticipation of having a good night’s rest. Their trip from Minnesota had taken them to the French Quarter in Louisiana, where Helen had been born. 
To their surprise, the room was quite neat. The bed sheets were folded well on both beds, a nice lamp in the middle. The couple had been tired, so they quickly unpacked their luggage and retired to their beds. It was comfortable and warm. It felt safe. They said their good nights to each other, and fell asleep, putting their long days behind them. 
Helen could not fall asleep however. Her thoughts of Frank were persistent. She had fallen in love with the love of her life. The two had only met in university, but three short but amazing years later, they had gotten married. Helen looked up to the ceiling, thinking about their wedding and everyone she had met. She fantasized what her life would be like from now on. Getting a job, moving into a house, and starting a family.
Knock. Knock. It was 1:00 AM. Who could that be? Helen slowly got out from under her blanket and cautiously walked toward the door to not wake up Frank. As she approached, she had a strange feeling in her stomach. She looked through the peephole and saw…high heels. Black high heels, polished, and new. However, they had a luminescent glow around them, almost…see through. Helen couldn’t see anyone around and didn’t know who knocked. She wanted to wake Frank, but he was out cold. Helen picked up the courage to open the door. Her hands were trembling to the lock, and slowly descended to the knob. Creak. Helen looked left and then right across the hallway, but no one was seen. Relieved, Helen looked down to the heels, but they were gone. 
“Frank!” Helen screamed
Frank shot out of bed, still groggy, but awake. 
“Frank, we need to leave now.”
“Why?”
“Something is wrong with this hotel. I don’t know what but…we have to go.”
“Alright.”
They hurriedly packed their belongings, quickly throwing their clothes into their luggage. Helen was quick to run toward the door and shut off the lights. 
Blood. On the door, with the same see-through glow like the heels. It was splattered across the door like someone had…coughed it up, covering the entire door. Helen’s eyes widened, a cold sensation traveled across her body. Fear. 
“Helen.”
Helen turned her head. Frank was sprawled on the ground, his face devoid of color. He coughed. A drop. Then two. A stream began coming out of his mouth. 
“Frank!” 
Helen rushed toward her husband’s side. Her passion for Frank was inextinguishable. She picked up Frank with all her might, and unlocked the door. She heaved Frank, one step at a time through the corridor. Helen was struggling. And then she looked up. 
A white figure was dressed in a beautiful wedding gown. Her face was beautiful, her skin delicate and fair. But her dress was ripped, her hair in tatters, and most jarring of all, a small knife in her heart. 
“Helen…”
Helen looked back down at Frank. His head was sagged backwards, his face completely pale. Helen held back a tear. The ghost drifted beside her, watching Helen tremble. She was going to lose everything, herself, her future, Frank. The ghost pulled the knife with the distinct glow out of her heart. Helen closed her eyes.
Shing. 
Helen had expected a sharp pain in her body, but it never came. Instead, when she opened her eyes, the ghost, with its lifeless eye and remorseless stare, dropped the knife in front of Helen. The knife’s glow faded, becoming…real. The ghost’s faced slowly morphed into sadness. Or was it pity?
